proposition.claim:
Here \(\mathbb R\) is Baire space \(\mathbb N^\mathbb N\). Write \([s]=\{x:s\preccurlyeq x\}\) for a basic cylinder. According to p. 328 (PDF 16), a game tree has no terminal nodes, a player moving outside it loses immediately, and a quasi-strategy for I must leave all II moves unrestricted. This last requirement is the decisive one below.

The full Wadge reduction definition on p. 329 (PDF 17) requires both sides of the membership equivalence, not just preservation of positive membership. Definable classes in Definition 3 require effective uniform coding of continuous preimages. These coding conditions are essential over \(\mathsf{RCA}_0\); external descriptions of ordinal classes must not be substituted for internally available codes without justification.

Equation reference: eq:layer. Definition 9, p. 335 (PDF 23), requires the compatibility \[
 W=\bigcup_i(A_i\cap C_i)\cup\bigl(B\setminus\bigcup_i C_i\bigr),
 \qquad W\cap C_i=A_i\cap C_i.\] The layers need not initially be disjoint. Lemma 10 disjointifies the \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^0_\xi\) layers; for \(\xi=2\), enumerating their closed pieces and assigning each point to its first piece verifies the required reduction. The compatibility in [eq:layer] (#eq:layer) is precisely what preserves the payoff on overlaps.

Theorem 69, p. 362 (PDF 50), takes a union \(\Gamma=\bigcup_l\Gamma_l\) of definable, effectively treeable classes, with \(\Gamma_{2l+1}=\check\Gamma_{2l}\). It relates \(\operatorname{LU}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^0_2,\Gamma)\) determinacy and strategic replacement to \(\Gamma\)-SR plus the union-operator monotone-induction principle of Definition 65. The latter is not merely the scheme \(\forall l\,(\Game\Gamma_l\text{-MI})\). The proof explicitly uses the paired dual classes in the reversal. Lemma 72 is needed in the forward direction and in identifying the winning-position set used for comprehension in (5.2).

Theorem 91, p. 380 (PDF 68), has additional projective-complexity and \(\beta\)-model hypotheses. Theorem 94, p. 381 (PDF 69), is a restricted reversal requiring \(\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_3\) transfinite induction; Conjecture 93 is not a proved general reversal. Likewise, the one-way classification list in Theorem 164, p. 423 (PDF 111), does not claim that every listed case is non-transferable. Its stated open cases must be retained. Theorem 175, p. 429 (PDF 117), is a boldface ZFC transfer theorem, uses ordinary Borel determinacy, and does not claim its lightface analogue. The limitations on replacing \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^0_2\) by \(\boldsymbol{\Pi}^0_2\) were checked at the level of the displayed reductions in Propositions 180–182; their external consistency-strength inputs were not reproved.

Q={q: some prefix lies in P or q lies in T(C_i,n)} is an I-quasistrategy; an I-winning strategy in the restricted W_i,n(P) game would win unrestricted.
